context_metadata.purpose: Compact routing context and reasoning gates. This is not the full OS and does not duplicate full record bodies.

purpose_and_boundary.purpose: JavaScript reasoning for practical internal tools, with a major Google Apps Script runtime-translation layer.
purpose_and_boundary.central_rule: JavaScript language reasoning transfers. Runtime assumptions do not automatically transfer.
purpose_and_boundary.book_authority: Eloquent JavaScript, Fourth Edition is authoritative only for source-supported JavaScript reasoning and source-era examples.
purpose_and_boundary.current_behavior_rule: Current project code, logs, runtime behavior, Google documentation, deployment settings, and SOPs outrank source-era platform assumptions.

authority_order: Current project code and runtime behavior
Current error logs, execution logs, stack traces, and user reports
Current browser and Node.js documentation when relevant
Current business requirements, SOPs, and workflow rules
Source-supported JavaScript concepts from Eloquent JavaScript
runtime_boundary_rules: JavaScript language reasoning transfers more reliably than runtime assumptions.
Google Apps Script is not Node.js.
Server-side Apps Script .gs code is not browser JavaScript.
DOM, browser events, form-element APIs, and browser storage apply only to HTMLService client-side code when currently supported.
Browser fetch is not UrlFetchApp; HTTP concepts transfer, API contracts and security contexts differ.
Node filesystem, HTTP server, stream, CommonJS, and NPM behavior do not transfer directly to Apps Script.
google.script.run is a client/server asynchronous boundary whose current behavior must be verified.
Apps Script service calls in .gs may look synchronous, but quotas, timeouts, external latency, concurrency, and partial effects still matter.
Current quotas, scopes, trigger behavior, deployment, uploads, permissions, services, modules, and security must be verified from current evidence.
The book never overrides current project code, logs, runtime behavior, or business rules.
non_negotiable_agent_rules: Identify the runtime before recommending code.
Inspect current project code, logs, data shape, deployment settings, and user reports before diagnosing a live tool.
Separate parse, validate, transform, export, UI, logging, and side-effect stages.
Validate data shape before writing to Sheets, sending mail, creating files, or calling an external write API.
Prefer a deterministic dry-run action plan before live mutation.
Do not hide unknown defects behind broad catch blocks.
Do not assume browser APIs work in server-side Apps Script.
Do not assume Node APIs or packages work in Apps Script.
Do not assume current Apps Script quotas or APIs from memory.
Do not treat fetch and UrlFetchApp as interchangeable.
Do not recommend DOM code inside .gs.
Do not recommend packages without verifying compatibility, build/deployment, license, security, and maintenance.
Do not claim a workflow works without tests and runtime evidence.
Do not invent current project code, schemas, mappings, permissions, or SOPs.
apps_script_reasoning_gate: What problem is the script solving?
What code runs client-side and what runs server-side?
What Apps Script service or runtime behavior is involved?
What side effects happen, and when?
What error should the user see?
What should be logged for the developer?
Is there a dry-run path before live write?
What current Google documentation must be verified?

workflow_stage_model.separation_rule: Service reads/writes, mail, file creation, and external HTTP effects must not be hidden inside row-level transformation helpers.
workflow_stage_model.partial_failure_rule: Represent success, rejected, skipped, failed, unknown-outcome, and retryable states explicitly; never collapse mixed results into one boolean.

generally_transfers: Regex semantics subject to runtime version

does_not_establish: Availability of Node APIs or NPM packages in Apps Script

current_verification_trigger_index.why: Apps Script runtime versions, supported syntax, built-ins, optimization, and edge behavior can change independently of the book.
Numeric quotas, reset windows, account tiers, payload limits, and execution limits are platform- and time-sensitive.
Trigger types, event objects, identity, authorization, schedules, concurrency, and failure reporting are host-specific and may change.
Version, deployment, execute-as, access, URL, rollback, and manifest behavior are platform settings that can change.
Scopes, consent, admin policy, deployment identity, and service access depend on current project/account configuration.
Sandbox, embedding, origin, script, navigation, security, and browser support can vary by platform release and deployment.
Supported argument/return values, handlers, error behavior, and client/server constraints are Apps Script-specific and time-sensitive.
Allowed payloads, Blob/form serialization, size limits, encoding, permissions, and HTMLService restrictions are platform-specific.
Raw/display/formula values, date objects, rectangular writes, limits, protections, and performance are current service behavior.
Drive ownership, shared-drive support, permissions, file conversion, Blob handling, and quotas are service-specific and time-sensitive.
Options, redirect behavior, certificate/security, response handling, scopes, payload limits, and quotas are current host behavior.
Scope, size limits, quotas, consistency, access identity, and serialization patterns are current service behavior.
Eviction, expiry, size, scope, quotas, and consistency are current platform behavior; cache must not be assumed durable.
Lock types, acquisition/timeout behavior, scope, quotas, and interaction with triggers are host-specific.
Quotas, authorization, sender identity, aliases, attachments, delivery behavior, and HTML restrictions can change.
Encoding, Blob/archive/conversion, formatting, and cryptographic helper behavior are current service/API facts.
Browser support, security restrictions, accessibility behavior, and API details evolve independently of the source.
Request/response options, streams, credentials, abort behavior, browser support, and security behavior can change.
CORS, content security, cookie/credential, mixed-content, origin, and HTMLService interactions evolve and are deployment-specific.
Node versions, globals, standard modules, stream behavior, security defaults, and deprecations can change.
Versions, maintenance, transitive dependencies, licenses, vulnerabilities, module format, and build compatibility change.
Apps Script runtime support, file loading, bundling, libraries, and tooling can differ from browsers/Node and change over time.
Runtime, project, spreadsheet, account, browser, locale, and company fiscal-calendar settings can produce different interpretations.
Admin restrictions, file sharing, external access, OAuth controls, and user roles vary by organization and change.
Project code, report schemas, mappings, business rules, dependencies, credentials, deployments, and observed errors can change at any time.
Endpoints, authentication, schemas, status semantics, pagination, rate limits, and deprecations are provider-specific and time-sensitive.
Column names, encodings, accepted formats, date windows, identifiers, and import validation rules are external and versioned.
Library compatibility, license, vulnerabilities, memory behavior, module format, bundling, and workbook feature support change.

Runtime boundary: Is this failure caused by JavaScript language behavior, Apps Script API behavior, or the business data shape?
Runtime boundary: For each non-language global name used here, which runtime or host API defines it?
Values and types: Is this value null, undefined, an empty string, zero, false, or a blank spreadsheet cell represented by the current API?
Values and types: What are the exact operand types immediately before this comparison, addition, or logical expression?
Program structure: What side effect, if any, occurs while this expression or condition is evaluated?
Control flow: What variable or state change proves this loop advances toward termination for every branch?
Functions: Can this function’s input contract, output, side effects, and failure behavior be stated in one sentence each?
Functions: Which outer bindings does this callback or returned function capture, and can any of them change before invocation?
Functions: What maximum recursion depth follows from the largest valid input, and is an iterative form safer?
Data structures: Which function mutates shared state, and which other references observe the same object or array?
Data shape: What exact object shape does each row have immediately after parsing and normalization?
Data shape: Do normalized headers remain one-to-one, or do two source columns collapse to the same property name?
Data integrity: What evidence proves input rows equal accepted plus rejected plus intentionally deduplicated or skipped rows?
Data shape: Does every output row have the exact same column count and ordering required by the destination?
Abstraction: Would a named map/filter/reduce operation make the transformation clearer, or would an explicit loop expose necessary control flow and diagnostics?
Higher-order functions: What invariant describes the reduce accumulator after processing the first n records?
Object design: What invariant, lifecycle, or substitutable behavior would a class enforce that a plain object plus functions would not?
Object methods: What call expression sets this for the failing method invocation?
Serialization: Which required fields and types change or disappear after JSON.stringify followed by JSON.parse?
Side effects: What external side effect occurs first, and which validations can still fail after it?
Error handling: For each catch block, which exact condition can this layer recover from without hiding an unexpected programming error?
Error handling: Is this error user-facing, developer-facing, or both, and what information belongs in each channel?
Error handling: If one item fails after others succeed, what status, evidence, and retry set are returned?
Error handling: Which state should be impossible after validation, and where should an assertion stop the workflow if it occurs?
Debugging: What is the smallest input, function path, and runtime context that reproduces this failure?
Testing: What exact expected rows, totals, statuses, and side effects form the test oracle for this case?
Live safety: Can this live write be represented and reviewed as an immutable dry-run action plan first?
Live safety: What stable operation key proves that a retry or duplicate event refers to the same logical action?
Regular expressions: Which realistic near-miss filenames or strings must this regex reject, and do anchored tests prove that?
Regular expressions: Could a greedy repeated part consume a delimiter or field that a later group is supposed to match?
Dates: Is this source value an instant, a local calendar date, a spreadsheet serial, or a formatted display string?
Dates: What test cases cover year-end, leap day, DST where relevant, and a 53-week fiscal year?
HTMLService boundary: Which exact functions run in HTMLService client JavaScript and which run in server-side .gs?
google.script.run: What serializable argument and result shape crosses google.script.run, including validation, partial, and failure states?
UI events: What happens if the user clicks submit twice, presses Enter while clicking, or retries after a slow response?
UI async: What happens if an older server request completes after a newer request and tries to update the same UI state?
UI state: Does every success, validation rejection, server exception, and transport failure transition the UI out of processing state?
Form validation: What happens when the server receives a payload that bypasses or tampers with every client-side validation rule?
File uploads: When one selected file fails validation, which user-entered fields and valid selections remain visible and recoverable?
HTTP boundary: Is this request executed by browser fetch or server-side UrlFetchApp, and why is that location required?
HTTP integration: Which status codes, response content types, and error bodies are handled explicitly before parsing or retrying?
HTTP integration: If the request times out after the remote system may have completed it, how is the actual outcome reconciled before retry?
Platform limits: What current Apps Script quota, service limit, payload limit, or execution limit could this measured workload consume?
Triggers: Which exact trigger type invokes this function, and what event fields, identity, authorization, concurrency, and failure reporting are currently verified?
Concurrency: What invariant is protected by the lock, what is the narrowest critical section, and what still prevents duplicate external effects?
Permissions: Who executes this path, whose file/mail/data is accessed, and which current scope and deployment setting authorize it?
Modules and deployment: Does this project need a runtime module loader, a build-time bundle, or only clearer file/function boundaries?
Deployment: Which exact code version, manifest/settings, deployment ID, and access policy are live, and how is the previous known-good version restored?
Mappings: Does each raw location label resolve to exactly one active canonical location under the current brand/context registry?
Dashboard metrics: What raw numerator, denominator, population, date range, and freshness timestamp support this displayed metric?
Email/report effects: What evidence proves the recipient list, privacy gate, attachment, and report version are correct before this send?
Uploaded files: Does the file content and parsed structure match the claimed extension, MIME hint, selected report type, and schema version?
Spreadsheet safety: Which imported fields can contain user-controlled text, and how does the destination distinguish literal text from formulas?
Observability: What minimum run ID, input/config fingerprint, stage counts, effect references, and sanitized error context are needed to investigate without storing sensitive payloads?
Current project evidence: What do the current project code, execution logs, stack traces, deployment settings, and representative user reports show before any recommendation is made?
Current verification: Which claim in this recommendation depends on current Apps Script, Workspace, browser, Node.js, quota, security, or deployment behavior?

completion_gate: Observed behavior or a reproducible fixture is available.
Language concept and host-specific behavior are separated.
All validation precedes live effects or an explicit consistency policy exists.
Expected rows, totals, status, and effect counts are defined.
